subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw core own pace-aware Anthropic/autonomous-agent throttling, and should the first accepted scope be read-only pace visibility or enforcement?
rationale: The issue adds provider-specific usage semantics, persisted runtime state, new config/defaults, status/session_status output, and autonomous-agent policy; automation cannot safely choose that product/API boundary.

options.title: Scope Read-Only Pace First
options.body: Expose pace projection in status/session_status without blocking work, then evaluate enforcement after users and maintainers validate the semantics.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Resource Governance
options.body: Keep this issue open but implement it only as part of a larger outbound rate-limit, budget, and provider-pool design across related issues.

options.title: Defer Core Enforcement
options.body: Keep core to usage hooks/status visibility and ask for plugin or external-policy work until a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Scope Read-Only Pace First
recommendation.body: Expose pace projection in status/session_status without blocking work, then evaluate enforcement after users and maintainers validate the semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is product/config direction across provider usage, status, auth-profile state, and resource-governance scope, where steipete has the strongest path-history and related-tracker signal.
